strengths: UniAP addresses a useful training-systems problem by jointly selecting pipeline partitions and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies under memory constraints. Explicitly modeling communication across stage boundaries is well motivated, and the ViT and Swin experiments establish relevance to computer vision.

The reported practical gains are meaningful. Table 2 shows 1.10–1.70× higher throughput than Galvatron across four models on EnvB. On EnvA, UniAP matches throughput for three models while reducing search time by 10.62–16.83×, and finds a runnable Swin strategy where Galvatron encounters OOM.

The ablation and case study provide useful interpretation. BERT benefits substantially from combining parallelism modes, and Appendix D illustrates how the selected strategy accounts for interconnect topology and memory limits. Hardware configurations, batch sizes, measurement windows, and solver settings provide a useful foundation for reproduction.
weaknesses: The published formulation does not enforce pipeline-stage order. Contiguity constraints permit a two-layer chain u→v to place u in stage 2 and v in stage 1. Equation (3) then assigns zero communication cost to that edge because it only counts forward connections between consecutively numbered stages. Edges skipping stages in a general DAG are also unaccounted for. These omissions can change the selected optimum and constitute a material correctness concern, rather than merely a presentation issue.

The claimed MIQP contains fourth-degree terms as written: expanding Equations (2)–(3) produces products such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl. No auxiliary-variable reformulation or equivalent solver-ready encoding is supplied. Standard transformations could address this, but the manuscript leaves an essential part of its main technical contribution unspecified.

The global-optimality and complexity claims exceed the evidence. Appendix C permits termination after 60 seconds or after 15 seconds with a relative optimality gap below 4%, yet achieved gaps and solver certificates are not reported. Treating solver runtime as a capped constant in Section 3.6 does not establish the complexity of finding an exact optimum. Moreover, any guarantee would apply only to the enumerated GPipe configurations and modeled costs, not unrestricted parallel training strategies.

The cost model is not quantitatively validated. Equation (1) excludes communication stages from the steady-state bottleneck and relies on aligned forward/backward bottlenecks; Section 3.3 additionally assumes linear scaling with batch size and backward computation approximately twice forward computation. No prediction-error or strategy-ranking measurements establish whether these approximations remain reliable across the tested interconnects and micro-batch sizes. Optimizing this surrogate therefore does not establish optimal measured throughput.

The experiments do not isolate the benefit of unified optimization. The Galvatron comparison changes both the search procedure and communication modeling, while Table 3 compares against inter-only and intra-only spaces rather than hierarchical search over the same candidates and costs. Both vision models match the inter-only variant in that table. Comparisons with the discussed hierarchical alternatives, Alpa and Piper, are also absent. The measurements support practical benefits, but provide weaker support for the claimed explanation and superiority of the unified search.

Reproducibility and reporting have additional limitations. Strategy-dictionary generation and detailed resharding and memory-cost construction remain underspecified, and reported search time covers UOP without quantifying profiling overhead. Separately, Table 1 evaluates T5-Large-48 while Table 4 specifies only 16/16 layers, and Figure 4(b) labels search time as throughput. These reporting issues are correctable; the unresolved formulation correctness and optimality claims are what determine the weak-reject recommendation.
